anytime_first_td_scorer.rederivation_notes: My chain before reading the record: (1) participation gate (active, snap taken; protected void at halftime); (2) team TD pool, TD-not-FG, per team; (3) scorer allocation by yard line, goal-line role, personnel and teammate absences; (4) for KXNFLTEAMFIRSTTD the player is the team's first TD scorer, so P = P(team scores any TD) x P(player is first-TD scorer | team TD); for KXNFLFIRSTTDTEAM/KXNFLFIRSTTD a two-team race with a NONE strike and D/ST scores; (5) 2+ TD overdispersion; (6) time-to-first-TD for KXNFLFIRSTTDTIME; (7) kicker long-range distribution for KXNFLLONGESTFG (70+ yd season extreme), plus longest/shortest TD extremes. Required inputs: team TD mean, red-zone/goal-line shares, snap/injury status, opening possession (race only), drive durations (time). Differences: the author covers 1-5 well and adds xTD and goal-line personnel, but applies the game-first race (opening possession) to a contract that is the TEAM's first TD, has no drive-duration input for FIRSTTDTIME, and models none of LONGESTFG, LONGEST/SHORTESTTD, NEXTTD (live-state). Also leans on a market-implied team split as a primary pool input.

findings.text: Interaction 3 and stage s4 apply 'P(player first TD) = P(team first TD) x P(player | team first TD)' with opening possession/script as the lever. The sampled KXNFLTEAMFIRSTTD rules ('If DJ Moore scores the first touchdown for Buffalo') make the event the TEAM's own first TD; the opponent race and opening possession barely matter, only P(Buffalo scores any TD) does (the text: 'If no Buffalo touchdowns are scored in the game, the No Buffalo Touchdown market resolves to Yes'). nfl.opening_possession is rated KEEP_SECONDARY/primary-relevant for the wrong contract; the right factor is P(team >=1 TD) x first-TD allocation.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: confirmed from KXNFLTEAMFIRSTTD text ('scores the first touchdown for Buffalo'). Rewrote stage s4 and interaction 2 around P(team >=1 TD) x P(player | team first TD), added nfl.model_team_td_mean, and limited opening possession to game-first contracts in s4, its audit and the interaction.

findings.text: nfl.team_total_split is KEEP_PRIMARY (s2, interactions 2 and 5) although the catalog defines it as 'implied total and spread to team means' and the author concedes it is market-implied. Market-derived values are benchmarks, not inputs. The model-derived TD pool (offense/defense EPA, drives, red-zone) must be the primary input; no such team-TD-mean input is defined (new inputs only add player-level xTD).
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: nfl.team_total_split audited BENCHMARK_ONLY and removed from stages s2/s5, coverage, interactions 1/4, nonlinearity and data feeds; added market-free new input nfl.model_team_td_mean (drives x TD-per-drive) as primary TD pool in s2.

findings.text: KXNFLFIRSTTDTIME (live, TITLE_ONLY) and KXNFLFIRSTTDTEAM (RULES_TEXT, in this archetype) are the live homes of the first-TD-team/time mechanism, yet first_score_team_time_race is recorded NO_LIVE_SERIES and the drive-duration/time-to-first-TD inputs (nfl.drive_duration_by_outcome etc.) exist only there. This record has no input for time-to-first-TD, so for a live series the required time data is missing. Mis-mapping is not disclosed in unresolved.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: confirmed mis-mapping. Recorded KXNFLFIRSTTDTEAM and KXNFLFIRSTTDTIME in contract.series_mapping_issues as belonging to first_score_team_time_race (which owns the race and time inputs); stage s4 now states that this record models only the allocation factor for those games.

findings.text: Live series KXNFLLONGESTFG (RULES_TEXT, 70+ yd season extreme), KXNFLLONGESTTD, KXNFLSHORTESTTD, KXNFLLONGESTPLAY, KXNFLNEXTTD have no mechanism or inputs (u2 admits 'no input here covers them'). Kicker leg-range/attempt-distance distribution, altitude/dome, 60+ yd attempt frequency are required inputs that are absent; disclosure is not a substitute for an input list for a live rules-text series.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: the extreme-value series are mis-filed. Recorded KXNFLLONGESTFG, LONGESTTD, SHORTESTTD, LONGESTPLAY (NEW_ARCHETYPE_NEEDED: season_extreme_play_markets), season and career TD accruals (season_player_stats_and_leaders) and game TD counts (game_events) in series_mapping_issues; variants text now makes claims about them conditional. No kicker-range input is invented here.

findings.text: Environment is marked COVERED by nfl.proe and nfl.dst_td_hazard, but interaction 4 (wind regime switch) lists only proe, qb_rushing, rz_share: no wind/weather input id is attached to this archetype. The claimed regime-switch cannot be tested with the declared inputs; category coverage is overstated.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: added existing catalog input nfl.weather_pit to stage s3, environment coverage and the wind regime-switch interaction 3, plus a weather forecast dataset row in required_data with the forecast-vs-observed caveat.

findings.text: Settlement definition says player-level markets settle 'in the full game including overtime'. Overtime is stated in the sampled text only for KXNFLFIRSTTDTEAM and KXNFLDSTTD (and TDPROT's participation clause); KXNFLTEAMFIRSTTD text samples are silent on OT. That is inference presented as established; rules_verification is correctly PARTIALLY_VERIFIED but the settlement paragraph should say so.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: reworded contract.settlement_definition to say overtime is explicit only for KXNFLFIRSTTDTEAM, KXNFLDSTTD and the TDPROT participation clause and is an assumption for KXNFLTEAMFIRSTTD.

findings.text: Source claims: goal-line personnel trees need participation/personnel data (nflverse participation covers roughly 2016-2023 from NGS, later via FTN) - history is short for a 'tree inside the 5'; nflverse load_snap_counts exists but a 'load_inactives' feed is not something I can confirm (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED). Game-day inactives may require scraping ESPN/PFR.

nfl.td_rates and nfl.dvp are WEAK but still referenced in stage s3 input_ids; nfl.dvp is also in opponent_matchup coverage. Either drop from stages or justify. Opponent matchup coverage therefore rests on a WEAK input plus the market-flavored redzone.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: removed nfl.dvp and nfl.td_rates from stage s3 and replaced the opponent_matchup coverage with nfl.redzone and nfl.model_team_td_mean; td_rates is kept only as a shrinkage prior inside nfl.player_xtd.

combos_and_parlays.rederivation_notes: My chain before reading: a combo is an intersection of leg events on one latent game process (margin, total, pace, availability, weather); same-game legs are dependent through script, accounting identities (player TDs sum to team TDs, receiving yards bounded by team pass yards), and shared availability; cross-game legs near-independent. Required inputs: calibrated leg marginals from sibling archetypes, a joint model (simulator/copula) with regime-dependent dependence, per-leg and combo-level void/push/OT rules, fees. Hazards: unknown combo rules for a voided leg; legs of mixed OT treatment. Differences: the author matches this chain closely (dependence by margin regime, accounting constraints, void matrix). Weak spots: no live series and no verification that Kalshi NFL combo products exist/how they are named; benchmark-only market items fill an entire stage and an interaction; one nonlinearity is not a single-input response.

findings.text: No live series is mapped and the evidence pack has no rules. Kalshi's multivariate-event (KXMVE-style) combo products are the likely live form; whether the ledger omitted them (instead of none existing) is SOURCE_UNVERIFIED and not raised in unresolved. If they exist, leg-void/push/OT rules would be knowable and the CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS item may be removable; the 'all legs must win' premise is stated in settlement text as 'understood', not evidenced.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: ledger check found KXNFLPREPACKSGP (EXCLUDED_COMBO, rules 'All outcomes encompassed in a market must occur for the market to resolve Yes.') and KXNFLCOMBO (no listed market); settlement text, data source and u1 now cite this evidence and record both in series_mapping_issues; void/push stays ambiguous.

findings.text: Nonlinearity 'nfl.team_total_split: truncation and concavity in the leg count' is not a response shape of a single input; leg count is not an input and team_total_split is market-implied. Remove or replace with a real single-input shape (e.g. joint probability vs correlation at fixed marginals).
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: replaced the leg-count nonlinearity on nfl.team_total_split with a real single-input shape on nfl.corr (joint probability convex in mean pairwise correlation at fixed marginals, capped by the smallest marginal).

findings.text: Interaction 5 and stage s5 use only BENCHMARK_ONLY/CONTEXT items (m.fees, m.combo_pricing, m.orderbook_depth); this is execution economics, not game information, and the interaction is arithmetic (fees + leg count), not an input interaction. Keep as context but do not count toward the interaction requirement.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: replaced interaction 4 (fees, price, depth arithmetic) with a margin-mean x total-mean x script joint-distribution interaction among game inputs, and stage s5 now states it is execution economics that does not count as an input interaction.

findings.text: Interaction 1 states 'Favourite cover and QB passing yards positively linked in shootouts, negative in blowouts' without saying whose QB, while stage s2 says favourite-cover and QB-yards are negatively related (trailing QB). Sign claims are contradictory/ambiguous and untestable as written.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: interaction 0 and stage s2 now state whose QB each sign applies to (favourite QB positive in shootouts and negative in blowouts; trailing team's QB negative with favourite cover) and give the contrast that tests it.

findings.text: nfl.ratings (market-implied history, WEAK) and nfl.team_total_split remain the declared inputs for leg marginals in s1/s3 talent coverage; marginals should come from sibling-archetype model outputs, not market-implied ratings. Marginal-source input is therefore an undefined dependency on other archetypes.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: nfl.ratings and nfl.team_total_split audited BENCHMARK_ONLY and removed from stages, coverage and interactions; added market-free nfl.model_team_points_mean and recorded the sibling-model marginal dependency in stage s1 and unresolved u5.

first_half_and_quarter_totals.rederivation_notes: My chain before reading: period points = drives starting in the period x points/drive, with discrete lattice (0,3,6,7,8,10,...); Q1 few drives and receive/defer order; Q2 two-minute drill; Q3 half-opening drive for the deferring team; Q4 game-state/garbage time with OT excluded; 2H includes OT per rules; tie atoms for winner markets (1H/2H/quarter 'neither team wins' resolves via Tie strike); 1HFT is a joint of half result and full game incl. OT; BTTS per quarter and in every regulation quarter. Inputs: opponent-adjusted team efficiency, possession allocation, period-specific scoring rates, halftime-state mixture, kickoff rules, QB status, OT model for 2H/1HFT. Differences: author covers this well, including regulation vs OT inclusion by series and the misfiled KXNFLDRAFTQB. Issues are market anchoring, an OT input labelled context though three sampled live series need it, and a couple of rules-text over-readings.

findings.text: nfl.team_total_split is KEEP_PRIMARY as 'the whole-game anchor from which period expectations are allocated'; it is derived from implied total/spread, i.e. market-derived. Period markets then inherit the market's weather/lineup knowledge and the archetype's own declared environment category is NOT_APPLICABLE only because of this anchor. A model-derived game-level mean (from game_total inputs) must replace it as the primary anchor, otherwise the environment and availability channels are missing from the actual input list.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: nfl.team_total_split audited BENCHMARK_ONLY and replaced everywhere (stage s3, coverage, data feeds) by market-free nfl.model_team_points_mean as whole-game anchor; weather now enters through nfl.weather_pit so the environment channel is no longer excluded.

findings.text: nfl.ot_model is KEEP_CONTEXT, yet KXNFL2H, KXNFL2HTOTAL, KXNFL2HSPREAD explicitly include overtime ('2nd half (including overtime)') and KXNFL1HFT's game leg includes OT. For 4 of the sampled live series it changes the distribution; role should be secondary, with OT points/tie-after-OT as an explicit lattice term for 2H.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: confirmed from rules text ('2nd half (including overtime)' for KXNFL2H, 2HTOTAL, 2HSPREAD; 1HFT 'including overtime'). nfl.ot_model re-audited KEEP_SECONDARY, added to stage s4 and game-script coverage with an explicit OT points term for second-half contracts.

findings.text: Evidence entry for KXNFL1QTOTAL claims a drive crossing a quarter boundary 'is credited by the clock time of the score'. The rules text only says 'Only points scored during the 1st Quarter of play count'; attribution of a score at the clock boundary (and scoring after the gun on a free play) is inference, not stated.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: reviewer correct, the rules text only says 'Only points scored during the 1st Quarter of play count'; rewrote the rules_evidence 'establishes', stage s6 and the data-source text to drop the clock-time claim and added unresolved u7 for boundary attribution.

findings.text: Environment NOT_APPLICABLE justification (period effect small versus possession/script) ignores that in-game weather changes (rain/wind arriving in 2H) are period-specific and that no weather input exists in the archetype's list at all; at minimum a GAP with a weather-timing input should be recorded.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: environment changed from NOT_APPLICABLE to COVERED by existing nfl.weather_pit (stage s2, new forecast dataset); in-game weather timing recorded as DATA_UNAVAILABLE in unresolved u6.

findings.text: Source: nflverse schedules/pbp do not carry the coin-toss winner or receive/defer decision (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED); receive/defer history likely needs Pro-Football-Reference game info or manual capture. This feeds nfl.opening_possession (and drive allocation interactions 1 and 2). Required_data row 'Coin toss and kickoff records [nflverse free]' should not be taken as verified.

KXNFLDRAFTQB is disclosed as misfiled, but the draft-order mechanism is then left homeless: off_field_events marks nfl.draft_board WEAK and says draft markets live elsewhere (see off_field_events findings).
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: recorded KXNFLDRAFTQB in contract.series_mapping_issues as belonging to off_field_events, dropped its rules_evidence entry and the claim to cover it here; the draft mechanism and inputs are written in the off_field_events record.

first_score_team_time_race.rederivation_notes: My chain before reading: first-passage race over alternating drives: receive/defer sets possession order; per-drive multinomial (TD, FG, punt, turnover, safety) with first-drive scripting; time of first TD = sum of drive durations (skewed) until a TD; D/ST/return TDs and safeties pre-empt; NONE strike (no TD in game) small; race-to-N is a lattice over TD/FG/XP/2pt/safety packages; overtime TD counts for first-TD team per the sibling rule text. Inputs: per-drive outcome rates by drive index, drive duration, opening possession, kicker/XP, non-offensive score hazard, field position after kickoff. Differences: author matches closely and adds drive_outcome_by_index, duration, scoring packages, non-offensive hazard. Problems: the archetype is recorded with no live series though first-TD team/time series with rules text exist in the sibling archetype, a few inputs referenced are market-flavoured or undefined, and two sources are unverified.

findings.text: Rules_verification NO_LIVE_SERIES and empty rules_evidence, while KXNFLFIRSTTDTEAM (rules sampled: 'All touchdowns count for this market, including offensive, defensive, and special teams. If the first touchdown of the game is recorded in overtime, then the market for that team still resolves to Yes.') and KXNFLFIRSTTDTIME/KXNFLFIRSTTD are live series for exactly this mechanism, filed under anytime_first_td_scorer. The settlement paragraph paraphrases the sibling text without quoting it; the record should cite it and flag the mis-mapping as such, and the two archetypes must agree on which one owns first-TD time/team inputs.

Stage s5 and category distribution_variance rely on nfl.score_resid and nfl.team_total_split. score_resid is defined 'around market lines and key numbers' and team_total_split is market-implied; neither is in this archetype's audited input list for score_resid, so a market-derived input is used without an audit verdict. Race-to-N lattice needs model-derived scoring-package probabilities (which the author defines separately); remove the market-based ids from stage inputs.

Source SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: 'Coin toss, receive/defer and kickoff records [nflverse schedules + pbp, free]'. nflverse pbp lacks the toss winner/decision (only who kicked off), so deferral behaviour (nfl.opening_possession primary) cannot be built from the stated source; likely needs PFR game pages.

Interaction 1 ('benefits double') is loosely argued: receiving first and a high scripted TD rate are largely additive on first-drive probability; the true non-linearity is the survival product over later drives. Interaction 2 (drive_duration x pace x q_scoring) is a convolution, with q_scoring WEAK and pace flagged a poor proxy in the audit; not a real input interaction.

nfl.qb is used in s6 and category availability_news but is neither an audited existing input nor a new input here; Nfl.team_total_split is audited WEAK yet listed as feeding data. Id bookkeeping is inconsistent.

Overtime-specific mechanism (first TD only in OT, OT kickoff rules under the 2025+ both-possessions regime) is not given an input; 'NONE'/OT mass for 'first TD never in regulation' affects KXNFLFIRSTTDTEAM pricing and is only a one-line variant.

game_events.rederivation_notes: My chain before reading: tie = regulation tie x P(level after OT) with lattice mass at zero margin and late-game management; OT market (KXNFLOT) = regulation tie only; safety = rare event driven by end-zone plays (sacks, punts from own end zone, holding) with team/QB/OL/punter factors; weekly tie = union across slate; longest rush = max of N carries, heavy tail; D/ST TDs are a separate hazard (live in sibling archetype). Inputs: margin/total model, OT rules regime (2025+ both teams possess), kicker/weather in OT, pass rush vs protection, punter/field position, carries and explosive-rate. Differences: author reaches the same chain and adds good inputs. Problems: undisclosed archetype mis-mapping of KXNFLLONGRSH and ignoring the TD-count/team-stat families; market-flavoured primary inputs for tie.

findings.text: Tie/OT stages (g1, g5, interaction 1) are built on nfl.score_resid ('residual around market lines and key numbers') and nfl.team_total_split (market-implied), both KEEP_PRIMARY/SECONDARY. P(tie) needs a model-derived margin lattice; as written the primary inputs for the headline series (KXNFLTIE, KXNFLWEEKTIE, KXNFLOT) are market-derived values.

KXNFLLONGRSH (player prop: longest rush of a named RB, ledger-mapped here) drives stage g4 and three new inputs (rush_yardage_tail, carry_count_forecast, carries/rb_efficiency) although it belongs to the rushing archetype (reviewed elsewhere). The mapping is not disclosed as a mis-mapping, and the families TOTAL_TD, PERIOD_TD, TEAM_STAT, GAME_STAT named in the archetype target have no mechanism and no unresolved entry; the archetype claims coverage of 'both teams score, TD counts, team stat thresholds' that the record never models.

u1 correctly marks the 2026 OT format as unverified; but P(level|OT) is the dominant tie input and the record gives OT hazard only by simulation. I could not confirm the current regular-season OT rule (both teams possess) from the record; treat as SOURCE_UNVERIFIED and treat the OT margin lattice (1-8 point margins, not just 3/6) as part of it.

KXNFLOT is TITLE_ONLY; the settlement says it is 'the regulation-tie event itself' - inference from the title, not rules text. Likewise KXNFLTIE text never says ties occur only after OT; that is domain knowledge.

Environment COVERED by weather_pit (context) with interaction 5 'effect only in extreme weather': a threshold effect applied to a base-rate-driven event; nfl.fumble_luck/turnovers WEAK items remain in the list and category counts.

Source: pbp-based end-zone exposure (yardline_100>=95) and safety flags exist in nflverse, but pressure-level data for per-play safety probability needs charting (PFF/NGS), not 'pbp free'; label SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for pressure-driven safety rates (u4 partially admits).

game_moneyline_spread.rederivation_notes: My chain before reading: final margin = team quality diff (QB-weighted) + HFA + situational shifts, with lattice noise (3/7/10 atoms), heteroskedastic SD by total/weather/QB, heavy tails for deep rungs; moneyline = P(margin>0) with tie handling by wording; spread rungs = nested tails; win-margin buckets = exact margin lattice incl. OT (rules say 'full game (including overtime)'); season/week series (KXNFLBLOWOUT, WEEKGAMEHIGH) = maxima over slate; division winners and novelty series are season/other mechanisms. Inputs: model-based ratings, lineup layer (QB, OL, pass rush), rest/travel, venue, weather, motivation, OT. Differences: author is close, adds lineup-adjusted rating, heteroskedastic SD, tail model. Main faults: market anchors leak in as inputs, OT is unverified for spread/ML, and many live series in the ledger (division winners, viewership) get no mechanism.

findings.text: Market-derived values used as inputs: nfl.ratings stays KEEP_PRIMARY even though the author notes 'market-implied history component makes it a benchmark'; the new nfl.heteroskedastic_margin_sd is fit on 'closing spread (as location only), total_line' and its raw_data lists closing lines; nfl.score_resid is KEEP_PRIMARY 'must be re-expressed around model means'. Closing lines in the feature set make the SD/tail inputs pregame-market dependent; required data should be model mean and model total only (lines kept for evaluation).

Live division-winner series (KXNFLAFCEAST/NORTH/SOUTH/WEST, NFC*), KXNFLVIEWERSHIP, KXNFLGAMELOCATION, KXNFLCELEBRITYGAME, KXNFLLASTTOWIN, KXNFLPROBOWLWIN are the majority of this archetype's live series with RULES_TEXT for several (division winner, Jake Paul compete). Author lists them as 'mis-bucketed' (u2) but gives no inputs; division-winner markets in particular need season sim/tiebreak inputs and are not covered here or necessarily in season_win_totals_and_futures. Undisclosed whether another record owns them.

Settlement: KXNFLSPREAD and KXNFLGAME OT/tie handling is correctly flagged unknown. But stage m5 speaks of 'OT-inclusive and regulation-only contracts' as if both exist; no sampled side contract is regulation-only. Under the current OT rules the OT margin lattice is wider than '3 or 6, or 0' (a TD plus extra point when both teams possess), unaddressed.

nfl.coverage_scheme is DUPLICATE_OF def_personnel by 'defensive scheme' wording, while the same input is KEEP_SECONDARY in qb archetype and in the category coverage list for opponent_matchup here; officiating_rules NOT_APPLICABLE cites 'penalty and pace terms' that are not inputs of this archetype.

Source: lineup_adjusted_team_rating weights rely on PFF grades/ESPN win-rate (paid/unverified, u4 admits); the ridge on availability indicators needs consistent historical depth/injury vintages that nflverse does not hold (weekly final injuries, not daily vintages). Treat 'partial' pregame_knowable as optimistic.

game_total.rederivation_notes: My chain before reading: total = sum of points over ~22-26 possessions; plays from clock use and mutual tempo; points/drive from opponent-adjusted efficiency, field position, red-zone, kicker; weather thresholds (wind, cold), roof; QB/OL availability as mixtures; correlated lattice-valued scores with key numbers and heavy tails; overtime inclusion unstated for KXNFLTOTAL/TOTALPRECISE (24.5 and 98.5 rungs) so a mixture; 1H total is a period contract. Inputs: pace, drives, EPA, weather forecast vintages, venue, QB, OL, kicker, tail model, OT. Differences: author matches and adds total-plays model, weather response, tail model, OT increment. Faults: coaching/tempo left as a declared GAP though the catalog input exists, situational category covered by a WEAK input, weather pregame data unverified.

findings.text: Coaching/scheme is declared GAP ('catalog coaching id is not attached here') for a market whose first-order driver is plays per game and 4th-down/tempo policy; nfl.coaching exists in the catalog (used in sibling archetypes) and stage t1 even uses nfl.two_minute_tempo. Leaving a known-available input out and logging it as a gap understates the input list; coach-level tempo/aggression should be an attached secondary input.

Weather: nfl.weather_total_response is primary but its pregame inputs are forecast vintages that the author concedes are unarchived (u2); nflverse schedules give game-time observed wind/temp only. Historical fits would be on observed, not forecast, values, so measurement error is not estimable. The 'partial' label is right but the input is relied on as primary; record the required own-capture history length (a season of capture) as a blocking data requirement.

Situational category is COVERED only by nfl.divisional_familiarity, which the same audit calls WEAK; short week/rest, late-season starter rest/seeding effects on totals are not covered or declared a gap (game_moneyline_spread includes rest_travel and motivation_seeding).

Settlement: OT not stated for KXNFLTOTAL/TOTALPRECISE, correctly flagged; but 'both-teams-to-score' and 'BOTH_TEAMS_SCORE_N' families have no live series and no stage, so the label of the archetype overpromises. KXNFL1HTOTAL (period contract) is included in the evidence and handled by the other archetype (duplicate coverage not reconciled).

nfl.total_distribution_tail is fit 'conditioned on expected total in terciles'; the source of expected total is not defined (model vs line). Heavy-tail claim for 98.5 relies on author recollection ('by recollection') and is not sourced.

off_field_events.rederivation_notes: My chain before reading: off-field outcomes are decisions by owners/GMs, league offices and voter panels, settled by official announcements; coach-out is a calendar hazard (in-season losses, post-season spike) with 'announces' clause counting; 53-man roster is a constrained selection with IR/PUP exclusion; signings require official announcement (insider reports are not settlement); awards and lists are vote-share races with co-winner 1/N rules; draft markets are order/board models; novelty events (ads, delays, sellouts) are reference-class or scheduled facts. Inputs: news with reporter credibility, contract/cap, calendar hazard, coach hot seat, award voting mechanics, draft board, base rates. Differences: author covers hazards and voting well. Faults: the draft family is dismissed even though it is in the archetype label, and several live series have no model.

findings.text: nfl.draft_board is audited WEAK with reason 'No draft market is in the sampled series of this archetype; relevant only for draft contracts filed elsewhere', while the archetype label is 'Draft, coach, transaction and Super Bowl novelty events' and family NFL/DRAFT is one of its five. The live KXNFLDRAFTQB (rules text: 'If a player's position differs across source agencies...') was filed under first_half_and_quarter_totals, whose author sent it back here. The draft mechanism (pick order, trades, QB class ranking, positional counts) therefore has no owner and no inputs in either record.

Live rules-text series KXNFLT100 (rank #N on a player-voted list), KXNFLROLE (broadcast role), KXNFLEXECOTY ('Tie/Co-Winners' strike) and the DPOY/MVP/OPOY specials have no defined inputs: vote_outcome_model is a softmax winner model, but a #3 rank on the Top 100 is an ordering/position problem with prior-year rank as the main predictor, and the Tie/Co-Winners strike is not modelled.

Environment GAP (weather delay, stadium) and ownership-stake/ad/sellout series have no inputs; disclosed (u1, u4) but 13 series listed TITLE_ONLY means roughly half the archetype's live series are unmodelled. Super Bowl novelty family has no live series and is not mentioned as such.

nfl.cap_and_contract is KEEP_PRIMARY while 'irrelevant to award and vote markets'; role should be per-series. nfl.standings_sim is context but is the only talent input for coach hazards and awards; its construction (non-market ratings?) is undefined.

Source claims: Spotrac/OverTheCap and X/Twitter archives are scrape or own-capture with terms-of-service risk; the insider-report log is correctly DATA_UNAVAILABLE, but 'nflverse rosters/players' does not hold a transactions wire (SOURCE_UNVERIFIED for nflverse transactions).

player_availability.rederivation_notes: My chain before reading: game-day participation = medical ability x team activation x snap taken; injury recovery clock; practice sequence to Friday designation to Sunday inactive list; healthy scratches/rest; depth-chart first-start as a weekly hazard of QB change; next-team is free agency/trade; retired or unsigned players (the sampled KXNFLWEEKCOMPETE names Aaron Donald) need a comeback/signing path, not an injury path. Inputs: injury report vintages, designation calibration, inactive list, depth-chart vintages and publication, news, QB performance gap, snap role, roster/contract status. Differences: author builds a good injury-to-play chain and a QB-change hazard, but the injury chain does not fit most live series (WEEKCOMPETE retired player, NEXTTEAM, RETURN) and the comeback/roster-status path is not an input.

findings.text: Live KXNFLWEEKCOMPETE sample is 'Will Aaron Donald play in a Pro Football game in Week 1?' (a player outside the usual injury-report population); KXNFLRETURN/KXNFLNEXTTEAM are signing/retirement contracts. The mechanism and inputs are almost entirely injury-report to inactive-list; no input covers retirement/comeback status, free-agent signing, roster membership, or contract/IR-designation of a player not on a roster. u4 mentions NEXTTEAM and RETURN but not WEEKCOMPETE's retired-player case, and gives no input. Required inputs differ materially for these contracts, so the input list cannot be relied on for them.

Two of the eight live series (KXNFLFIRSTSTART, KXNFLDEBUT) settle on a published depth chart; the record's stage a4 treats it as a QB-change hazard but nfl.qb_change_hazard and the QB performance gap (talent_strength GAP) are undefined for rookies/unproven QBs. The category GAP is disclosed but it is a core primary input (incumbent vs challenger value, draft capital), listed primary with no measurable definition.

KXNFLDEBUT title says 'Player to Make Debut' while its sample settles as QB first start; author notes the mismatch but does not state that DEBUT itself might also have other (true debut) strikes unseen. Treat as CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS in unresolved (only EVERYWEEK/WEEKSTART/RETURN are there).

Sources: 'nflverse load_snap_counts and inactives' (no inactives loader I can confirm), 'nflverse rosters/transactions', and depth charts 'free' (weekly snapshots; chart-publication timing requires own capture) are SOURCE_UNVERIFIED; official injury practice-day vintages are acknowledged unarchived (u2).

nfl.in_game_exit_risk, nfl.snaps, nfl.rest_travel audited WEAK/irrelevant for the contracts but remain in stage inputs (a5, a3); category pace_volume/environment NOT_APPLICABLE is acceptable but the only situational input is motivation_seeding, which the audit says is irrelevant for weeks 7-10 windows.

qb_passing_tds_and_ints.rederivation_notes: My chain before reading: QB count = attempts x per-attempt rate; attempts from team dropbacks (pace, script, PROE, weather, run game) times QB share of snaps (starter status, blowout pull, in-game injury); TD = red-zone/goal-to-go dropbacks x pass share near goal line x conversion (receiver quality), regress TD luck; INT = attempts x INT rate (decision quality, pressure, depth, defender luck); overdispersion; ladders nested/monotone; fair-price void if no live play and protected halftime void; season/career versions add games played. Inputs: QB quality, team pass volume, goal-line pass rate, receiver availability, opponent pass rush/coverage, weather, blowout pull. Differences: author matches and adds xPassTD, goal-to-go rate, pull hazard, opponent INT propensity. Faults: verification overclaim, market-implied pool primary-adjacent, Kalshi listed as data source for non-market inputs, unverified charting sources.

findings.text: rules_verification is VERIFIED_FROM_RULES_TEXT although the archetype target is TDs and INTs and KXNFLPASSINT (the only INT series), PASSATT and CAREERPASSTDS are TITLE_ONLY (u1 itself says so). The settlement paragraph lumps 'KXNFLPASSTDS, PASSINT, PASSCOMP, PASSATT' as resolving 'at least N' with INT strikes '1+ and 2+ typically' - the INT rule text was never seen. Should be PARTIALLY_VERIFIED; INT wording (pick-six, penalty-nullified INT) is inference.

required_data row 'Kalshi ladders and rules [Kalshi API]' lists feeds_inputs nfl.team_total_split, nfl.qb_rushing, nfl.coverage_scheme. Kalshi data cannot feed QB rushing or coverage inputs, and feeding team_total_split from Kalshi/market ladders makes a market-derived value an input (the audit admits it is 'largely market-derived'). Data lineage is wrong; team TD pool must be model-derived.

nfl.qb_expected_pass_td measurement uses offense_personnel and defenders_in_box on '2006+ pass attempts'; those fields exist only in participation-era data (about 2016+), and the cited ff_opportunity expected-pass-TD fields are flagged unverified. Turnover-worthy throw rate and pressure-to-throw require PFF/SIS charting (u2), so the int_rate input (KEEP_PRIMARY) rests on non-public data; public proxy (INT rate vs air-yards/pressure from pbp-NGS) undefined.

nfl.qb (starter status) is used in stages q1 and availability coverage but is not among audited existing inputs for this archetype and not added as new; QB talent enters only via xPassTD and int_rate. Receiver/TE quality inputs are only skill_avail (secondary) although they drive per-attempt TD probability.

Situational GAP (QB rest in meaningless weeks) and officiating NOT_APPLICABLE (DPI spot fouls convert to goal-line TDs) are asserted without quantification; DPI is a real passing-TD route in the red zone and has an input in neither archetype.
